Based on my search, here's how to actually pronounce "doge":

## The Correct Pronunciation

**"Doge" is pronounced as /dəʊʒ/ (British) or /doʊʒ/ (American)** — essentially **"dohj"** or **"dohzh"** (rhyming with "beige").

This pronunciation was confirmed by **Jackson Palmer**, co-creator of Dogecoin, who stated the name was inspired by the animated series **Homestar Runner**. In a 2005 episode, a character spells out "D-O-G-E" and another character reads it as "dohj" /dəʊʒ/.

## Common Mispronunciations to Avoid

| Incorrect | Why It's Wrong |
|-----------|--------------|
| "Dog" | Missing the soft "j/zh" ending |
| "Doggy" | Adding an extra syllable incorrectly |
| "Dodge" | Wrong vowel sound and ending |
| "Dog-ee" | Treating the "e" as a separate syllable |
| "Dough-gie" | Adding an extra syllable that doesn't exist |

## The Two Meanings, Same Pronunciation

Interestingly, "doge" has two distinct meanings with the **same pronunciation**:

1. **The meme/cryptocurrency** — the Shiba Inu internet meme that became Dogecoin
2. **The historical title** — the chief magistrate of the former republics of Venice and Genoa (from Italian "Doge," derived from Latin "dux" meaning "leader")

Some sources note that in Italian, the historical title is sometimes pronounced closer to "Doh-jay," but in English contexts, both meanings use the same "dohj" pronunciation.

## IPA Breakdown

- **UK**: /dəʊʒ/ — "d" + "oh" (as in "nose") + "zh" (as in "vision")
- **US**: /doʊʒ/ — same sounds with the American "o" vowel

So if you want to say it correctly: **"dohj"** — one syllable, soft "j" or "zh" at the end, not a hard "g" sound.
